_about: Site-specific interpretive text for notebook 03's summary.json (Liwa). Every string is a Python format template filled from this run's numbers (vs, nd, ph, s30, l30, ws, qc, P, n_dunes, pct_below, tt: see the seih_al_hama file). Written after looking at this site's notebook 02 and 03 results; ranges quoted literally (heights) are from the 2026-11-15 run.

published.reference: Lorenz, Radebaugh, Barnes & Turtle, EGU2016-9369; Lorenz & Radebaugh 2015 (Planetary Dunes Workshop 8003); Pugh, Glennie & Williams 1993 (AAPG abstract)
published.their_value: ~0.1 m/yr for the 50-80 m Liwa megadunes (a field inference from overrun date palms, abstracts only); the smaller northern dunes 'migrate southward more rapidly than the draa' (no number)
published.our_value: megadune and other large-dune bodies: below the detection limit (median limit {qc[draa_bodies][detection_limit_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr) for all {qc[draa_bodies][n_valid]} bodies that could be tracked; small dunes and bedforms: {vs[detected_speed_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr median toward {ph[field_median_heading_deg]:.0f} deg (2013-2025)
published.note: Consistent, but not a test of the 0.1 m/yr: that rate is about a tenth of what this method can resolve here, so 'below the detection limit' neither confirms nor contradicts it. What the data do show is the published pattern: motion toward the south-south-east, and small dunes much faster than the megadunes they surround and ride on.

wind_agreement_note: mean |heading - RDD| over detected windows, RDD {ws[RDD_deg]} deg (MERRA-2 2000-2024). The regime is close to unimodal (RDP/DP {ws[RDP_DP]}): the field-median heading {ph[field_median_heading_deg]} deg is {ph[field_heading_minus_modes_deg][0]} deg from the strongest sand-moving mode (toward {ph[wind_mode_toward_deg][0]} deg) and {ph[field_heading_minus_RDD_deg]} deg from RDD; per-window median difference {ph[per_window_abs_heading_minus_RDD_median_deg]} deg. Year-to-year field speeds follow the MERRA-2 drift (r {qc[interannual][wind_correlation][pearson_r]}).
second_dataset_note: HLS S30 (Sentinel-2) agrees on direction (field headings {s30[heading_difference_deg]} deg apart) and partly on the pattern (r {s30[corr_E]} E, {s30[corr_N]} N), with lower speeds ({s30[field_median_speed_hls_myr]} vs {s30[field_median_speed_landsat_myr]} m/yr). HLS L30 (same Landsat instruments): heading within {l30[heading_difference_deg]} deg, {l30[field_median_speed_hls_myr]} vs {l30[field_median_speed_landsat_myr]} m/yr. Both HLS stacks are registered on the same date-palm farms as Landsat, so they share the possible registration bias described in the limits and do not test it.
limits: Detected dune windows move a median {vs[detected_speed_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr (10-90 %: {vs[detected_speed_p10_p90_myr][0]:.2f}-{vs[detected_speed_p10_p90_myr][1]:.2f}, max {vs[detected_speed_range_myr][1]:.2f}) toward {ph[field_median_heading_deg]:.0f} deg; {pct_below:.0f} % of valid dune windows move below the detection limit (median {nd[detection_limit_median_myr]:.2f} m/yr).

These speeds may be overstated by up to ~{qc[registration_check][trend_all_speed_myr]:.1f} m/yr toward the south-south-east. The only stable ground here is date-palm farms, whose apparent drift (toward {qc[registration_check][trend_all_toward_deg]:.0f} deg, the anti-sun direction, as growing palm shadows would cause) cannot be checked against unvegetated ground in this box; it is carried in the detection limit, not removed.

Megadune bodies (up to ~110 m of relief) are below the detection limit. The motion in the velocity grid, the dune polygons and the reach years is that of the small dunes and the bedforms riding over the megadunes, not of the megadunes themselves.

Reach years forecast the migration of dune forms (slip-face advance), not wind-blown sand crossing a road, which happens wherever a road borders loose sand, whatever the dunes do (see borders_free_sand in targets.geojson).
At about 1.8 m/yr one 15 m pixel is about 8 years of motion, so reach years for targets near the sand carry an edge uncertainty of +-7.5 m plus the outline uncertainty of the target.
Most targets are not reached by {P[projection_end]}; targets flagged 'sand at edge now' already have migrating sand within that edge uncertainty.
The projection is advection along the measured 2013-2025 motion, assuming those conditions continue; it does not model dune deformation, merging, splitting or growth.
Vegetation, windbreaks, sand fences, levelling, construction and climate change alter the outcome; many farm edges here are walled.

Motion is measured in 480 m windows: it is the motion of the small dunes (spacing ~{qc[linearity_aliasing][dune_spacing_25pct_variance_below_m]}-{qc[linearity_aliasing][dune_spacing_spectral_peak_m]} m) and sand sheets inside, not of a single dune body.
Only {n_dunes} dunes (13-31 m high) are outlined from NASADEM (February 2000) at bedform scale; they are medium dunes, mostly in the northern field, not megadunes.
The Sentinel-2 (HLS S30) check agrees on direction with lower speeds, but shares the farm-based registration and so cannot test the registration caveat.
The published ~0.1 m/yr for the megadunes is a field inference far below this method's detection limit here: no numeric comparison is possible.
MERRA-2 wind is a ~0.5 x 0.625 deg reanalysis of hourly means; absolute drift potential is approximate.
Farm targets are vegetated plots (HLS NDVI, last year) plus OSM farmland; built-up targets are OSM buildings and residential areas; unmapped or abandoned plots are not targets.
Results are valid for this box (the eastern Liwa crescent, not Liwa town) and 2013-2025 only; nothing outside the box is assessed.
